trends.what: A curated directory of hundreds of free APIs for developers to use in their projects.
trends.why: It's a one-stop reference for builders, constantly updated, making it the go-to starting point for any app or integration idea.

trends.what: An open-source platform offering a full curriculum and coding challenges to learn programming, math, and computer science for free.
trends.why: It remains the gold standard for self-taught developers, with a massive community and continuously expanding course content.

trends.what: A massive, community-maintained collection of freely accessible programming books, tutorials, and learning resources.
trends.why: It democratizes access to knowledge, saving learners hundreds of dollars and covering every language and topic imaginable.

trends.what: A personal AI assistant that runs on any OS and platform, designed to be your always-available digital helper.
trends.why: It's a bold, cross-platform take on local AI, promising privacy and control, which is a hot topic as users seek alternatives to cloud assistants.

trends.what: Interactive visual roadmaps and guides that outline step-by-step learning paths for various developer careers and technologies.
trends.why: It simplifies the overwhelming tech landscape into clear, actionable paths, making it essential for beginners and career-switchers.

trends.what: A tool that modifies AI agent behavior to generate minimal, lazy, and efficient code, mimicking a senior developer's 'less is more' approach.
trends.why: It's a humorous yet practical take on AI code quality, addressing the common problem of over-engineered AI-generated solutions.

trends.what: A fullscreen, mouse-interactive terminal user interface (TUI) and harness for running coding agents, designed for extensibility.
trends.why: It brings a modern, immersive, and interactive experience to terminal-based AI coding, appealing to power users who live in the CLI.

trends.what: A pure C, zero-dependency runtime that runs frontier mixture-of-experts (MoE) AI models by streaming experts from disk, enabling use on existing hardware.
trends.why: It promises to run state-of-the-art models on everyday computers without expensive GPUs, a major breakthrough for local AI accessibility.
